A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same autoencoder latent-dynamics study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original autoencoder training analyses, data-free reconstruction experiments, and out-of-distribution detection results, including supplementary experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in the main text and Appendix B.

M1.justification: Both versions iterate the same encoder–decoder composition to obtain attractors, use attractor dictionaries with OMP for reconstruction, and score latent trajectories for distribution-shift detection. The revised explanations introduce no procedural component.

E1.justification: Both retain the CIFAR/MNIST/FashionMNIST studies, six reconstruction datasets, and SUN397/Places365/Texture/iNaturalist OOD evaluations. Appendix B retains the same initialization, training, and reduced-dataset scenarios.

E2.justification: The reconstruction experiments retain the random orthogonal-basis comparator, and Figure 5 retains KNN. Newly discussed Neural ODEs and deep equilibrium models are related work, not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Both specify 4096 noise initializations and 500 test examples per reconstruction dataset, 2000 ImageNet reference samples and KNN neighbors for OOD detection, and the same metrics, training budgets, and convergence thresholds. No new evaluation protocol appears.

E4.justification: The regularization and training-dynamics analyses are retained. Appendix B preserves the initialization study, qualitative reconstructions, OOD histograms, convergence-speed validation, attractor-rank analysis, and dataset-size memorization study.

E5.justification: Both report means and standard deviations over attractors and specify ten initialization seeds in Appendix B.1. Error-bar practices and statistical reporting are unchanged.

E6.justification: The empirical plots, qualitative examples, and reported scores are retained. For example, Figure 5 reports SUN397 FPR/AUROC of 29.60/91.20 for attractor distances and 100.00/42.59 for KNN in both versions; Figure 11 retains the 0.67 convergence correlation.

T1.justification: v3 adds Proposition 3.2 and Appendix A.3, defining nearest-attractor projection and claiming prototype/coverage bounds on reconstruction error, including an epsilon-cover extension and proof. Equation 5 corrects the reversed Lipschitz inequality. The earlier convergence proposition survives in A.4–A.5. The new proof incorrectly drops the cross term when bounding a squared norm.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about latent vector fields, contraction, memorization/generalization, data-free weight probing, and distribution-shift detection. The new proposition provides attempted theoretical support without changing these headline claims.

C2.justification: v1 describes attractors as potentially nonlinear interpolations of training samples. v3 develops a prototype-accuracy and latent-coverage interpretation of generalization and links nearest-attractor projection to dynamical destinations. Existing limitations concerning extension beyond autoencoders remain.

D1.justification: Tables 1 and 3 and Appendix D retain the architectures, Adam settings, 500-epoch training budget, iteration limits, pretrained-model descriptions, NVIDIA 3080TI hardware, and PyTorch implementation information. No new code or data access instructions appear.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds positioning against Neural ODEs (Chen et al., 2018) and deep equilibrium models (Bai et al., 2019). The Places365 citation changes from López-Cifuentes et al. (2020) to Zhou and Paffenroth (2017). Most existing research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: The introduction, method exposition, theoretical discussion, and experimental descriptions undergo extensive rewriting. New subsections separate regularization from training dynamics, while linear/homogeneous examples and convergence discussion move into Appendix A. Cross-references and terminology are also revised.

P2.justification: The same fourteen figures and three numbered tables remain. Captions are refined, particularly for Figures 1 and 3, while typography, table sizing, and float placement change. Figure 5 and several appendix displays move without substantive redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 improves exposition and research positioning and corrects the Lipschitz definition. However, its principal theoretical addition, Proposition 3.2/Appendix A.3, relies on the invalid general inequality ||a+b||^2 <= ||a||^2 + ||b||^2, leaving the claimed bound unestablished. With empirical evidence unchanged, the clarity gains and newly introduced theoretical defect leave the net quality direction uncertain.
